attributes.body_ja:
「難（がた）い」は、動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）につながって、接尾語（せつびご）として使（つか）われる文法（ぶんぽう）です。漢字（かんじ）からもわかるとおり、「(A) をするのが難（むずか）しい」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。ほとんどの場合（ばあい）、「がたい」はひらがなで書（か）かれます。

「にくい」は「個人的（こじんてき）に抵抗感（ていこうかん）があって難（むずか）しい」という場合（ばあい）に使（つか）われます。その一方（いっぽう）で、「がたい」は「それをすること自体（じたい）が非常（ひじょう）に難（むずか）しく、（そうしたくても）そうできない」というニュアンスがあります。そのため、「がたい」は「にくい」よりも強（つよ）い表現（ひょうげん）で、それがほとんど不可能（ふかのう）に近（ちか）いときに使（つか）われます。

まとめると、

にくい ‐ 人の感覚（かんかく）や経験（けいけん）、状況（じょうきょう）によって、難（むずか）しいと感（かん）じる。

がたい ‐ それ自体（じたい）が難（むずか）しすぎて、そうしたくてもそうできない（ほとんど不可能（ふかのう））。
attributes.body:
Coming from the same kanji as 難（むずか）しい 'difficult', 難（がた）い is a suffix that also means 'difficult'. However, in the case of がたい, it will be attached to the conjunctive form of verbs, and conveys that '(A) is difficult to do'. がたい is almost always written without kanji in this meaning.

Compared to にくい, which can simply imply that something is 'uncomfortable' to do, がたい refers almost exclusively to 困難（こんなん）であること 'things that involve a high degree of difficulty, distress, or infeasibility'. Due to this, がたい will come across as far stronger than にくい, and may imply that a certain task is almost impossible.

Summed up, these nuances basically translate as the following:

にくい - Something is difficult based on someone's opinion, experience, or general feeling.

がたい - Something is difficult based on the task itself having a high level of difficulty.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: Describing actions as easy or hard
The difference between がたい、にくい、and づらい

attributes.body: がたい and にくい both attach to verb stems and express the idea of 'difficult to do', but with different nuance and formality levels. にくい is used in everyday speech and reflects the speaker's personal sense of difficulty or discomfort. がたい is more formal/written-style and implies something is nearly impossible or extremely difficult due to factors beyond the speaker's control.

Both ようがない・ようもない and がたい express difficulty or unfeasibility of an action, but differ in nuance. ようがない・ようもない conveys that there is no way or means to do something. For example, 連絡のしようがない ('There's no way to contact him'). がたい, on the other hand, indicates that something is very difficult to do, often due to factors beyond the speaker's control. For example, 信じがたい話だ ('It's a story that is hard to believe').
